extension.summary: YouTube TV live channels and on-demand for Kodi (experimental)
extension.description:
Watch the live channel lineup and on-demand catalogue from your own YouTube TV subscription, playing back through InputStream Adaptive with Widevine DRM.
EXPERIMENTAL: Google provides no public API for YouTube TV. This addon speaks the same private InnerTube endpoints as the YouTube TV web player, identifying itself as the WEB_UNPLUGGED client. Sign-in is by importing cookies from a browser already signed in to tv.youtube.com; Google does not permit scripted password login.
Playback depends on the DASH manifest that the player endpoint offers alongside its own SABR streaming URL. The web player itself always takes the SABR path, so the DASH route is documented but lightly travelled -- if Google stops serving it, this addon stops working and there is no fallback short of reimplementing SABR.
Features: * Live channel list and 7-day electronic programme guide * On-demand titles and search * Widevine playback via InputStream Adaptive, up to 1080p where the account allows * Local licence proxy handling YouTube's JSON-wrapped, rotating-key Widevine exchange
Your subscription, your account, your lineup. Nothing is proxied through a third party.
extension.disclaimer: Not affiliated with or endorsed by Google LLC. YouTube and YouTube TV are trademarks of Google LLC. This addon uses private, undocumented endpoints that Google's terms of service do not permit third-party clients to call; use it with your own subscription and accept the risk to your account.
extension.news:
2026.8.31.20 - The guide's whole schedule, on the TV client - Found it. The guide sends 989 airings and the add-on was reading 143. Only the airing currently on the air carries a watchEndpoint; the other 846 carry an unpluggedGetSidesheetCommand and no videoId field at all, the same mechanism the Library's tiles use. The programme's id is inside it, alongside the show's, and is now read. 143 airings become 989, a median of 7 per channel.
2026.8.31.19 - Find out why the guide has no schedule - On this account the guide comes back with one airing per channel, 143 for 148 stations, where the browser capture the reader was written from had 953. The continuation adds nothing. Both are now reported and the responses kept, so the difference can be read rather than guessed at. - The guide window is asked for on the hour, which is what both captures do and what this was not doing.
2026.8.31.18 - Channel order setting, rebuilt - Kodi stopped starting with 2026.8.31.17 installed, on both Kodi 21.3 and 22.0, with no stack trace in the crash log. The Channel order setting was the one thing that build added which Kodi itself parses, and it was the only list in settings.xml written as a string with an empty option value and allowempty beside options. It is now an integer with plain numeric values, exactly like every other list in the file.
2026.8.31.17 - Channel order - A Channel order setting, offering YouTube TV's own five orderings: default, the custom order arranged on the web, most watched, A-Z and Z-A. Left alone it changes nothing and the account's own choice decides. - The guide pages eight deep for the Kodi TV section rather than four. Pagination brings more hours, not more channels: every page carries the same lineup, and eleven pages took one lineup from 962 airings to 6306.
2026.8.31.16 - The guide's later pages - A later page of the guide names no channel: each row carries only a stationId and more airings, with no station renderer, so every airing past the first page was dropped. Reading the row's own id and merging takes the guide from 953 airings to 1555, a median of 10 per channel. - The Kodi PVR guide asked for one twenty-four hour window, a shape no capture covers. It now asks for four pages of six hours, which is what the web client does, and hands over 1555 programmes where it handed 148.
2026.8.31.15 - The Library reads in full - The TV client's Library tiles do not navigate anywhere: each carries an unpluggedGetSidesheetCommand that opens a detail panel, with no browseId field on the tile at all. The id is inside the command's params, base64 of a small protobuf, and is now read from it. Nine tabs, 26 tiles. - Checked against the web capture: on seven of the eight titles that appear in both, the id read out of the token is the same one the web client navigates to.
2026.8.31.14 - The guide's whole schedule - The guide showed what was on and nothing after it, on every channel. Page one holds 953 airings and only 144 were read: every airing carries its id in a plain videoId field, and only the one on the air also gets a watchEndpoint, which was the only place being looked. 953 airings now, a median of 6 per channel. - That endpoint is the guide's own word for "which one is on now", so it is recorded and preferred over comparing timestamps. Live channels resolves to the same programme as before on every station that had one.
2026.8.31.13 - Library items - The TV client's Library tiles carry a primaryText, a thumbnail and a navigationEndpoint, and were dropped anyway: what sits inside that endpoint is called neither watchEndpoint nor browseEndpoint. Any endpoint naming a videoId or a browseId is now followed, whatever it is called. One level down only, so a dialog's buttons and a tile's menu are still not rows, and an endpoint naming no id -- a buy prompt -- is still nowhere to go.
2026.8.31.12 - Say why a Library tab is empty - The diagnostic that was meant to explain an empty tab stayed quiet, twice over: it fired only when the whole page listed nothing, and one item in Scheduled was enough to silence it for the other eight tabs; and it asked for a title and a thumbnail before reporting a renderer, so a client filing those elsewhere reported as nothing at all. - Any empty tab now reports, and the fallback sampler asks for nothing: it lists what each renderer in the response actually carries. The page is written to library-shape.json again as well.
2026.8.31.11 - Library tiles - The TV client's Library named its nine tabs correctly and every one was empty, though the response holds 26 tiles. A tile's endpoint is now looked for under onSelectCommand, tapCommand and entityPageNavigationEndpoint as well as navigationEndpoint; every capture parses identically to before. - When a page answers and holds nothing readable, the keys its tiles carry are logged, which names the key to read next.
2026.8.31.10 - Station names and logos - Only 7 of 148 stations carry a name field; the rest are named by the accessibility label on their logo. That label and the logo are now searched for across the whole station renderer instead of under one key, so a client that files the logo elsewhere no longer loses both. - Guide and Live channels count nameless and logoless stations apart from dropped ones, and log the fields the stations actually carry.
2026.8.31.9 - The Library reads on the TV client - The TV client sends the Library in unpluggedLibraryContinuation with a chip row of nine tabs against nine cells, where the web client sends a section list with filter and sort dropdowns and their cross product. Both are read now, and the pairing is checked against the cell count either way. - Asking as the web client instead is not an option: the bearer is refused for it with HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. That retry is gone. - Guide and Live channels now say what they drop and why: how many stations parsed, how many carried no airings, and how many have a programme with no video id, naming them.
2026.8.31.8 - Library on the TV client - The Library grid was read off a web-client capture and the TV client answers with a different container: 0 rows, 0 filters, one item listed. Rows are now also found by shape, with no container name needed, the Library is retried as the web client when the first answer cannot be read, and an unreadable page is written to library-shape.json in the add-on's profile directory so the real shape can be seen.
2026.8.31 - Home and Library - Home: the front page YouTube TV builds for the account -- Resume watching, Top picks for you and the twenty genre rows behind them, each row a folder. - Library: recordings, purchases and scheduled recordings, with the account's own Shows / Movies / Sports / Events / Purchased filters as folders. - A scheduled recording that is on the air now is playable. It carries no watchEndpoint, only a "Join live / Start from beginning" dialog with one inside, so it used to be dropped from the listing altogether. - Two airings of one show are two rows again, with the time in front of the title. Deduplicating on destination alone had collapsed them into one.
2026.8.28 - Key ids carried between plays - The licence response names a key id per track type; ISA never had one, and opened every session with an unknown KID. Those ids are now recorded and supplied through pre_init_data on the next play of the same title.
2026.8.27 - First cut - Live channel list and EPG from browse(FEunplugged_epg), on-demand and search, Widevine playback through a local licence proxy. Playback is unverified pending a check that the DASH manifest actually serves; see docs/youtube-tv-protocol.md.
